items.body:
Fixes #5765.

Sync `Field.Control` and `Input` filled state with the native value after form reset. Covers nonempty defaults, canceled resets, external forms, controlled values, and an input replaced by a reset handler without emitting `onValueChange`.

Validation passed: related jsdom tests (1,145), Field/Input/Form browser tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (342 per engine), `pnpm typescript`, `pnpm eslint`, `pnpm stylelint`, and `pnpm prettier`. The reset regression tests fail on the unchanged base.

- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

items.title: [field] FieldControl warns about a changing defaultValue that it already handles correctly

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
# Bug report

## Current behavior

`Field.Control` / `Input` log a dev warning whenever `defaultValue` changes after mount:

> Base UI: A component is changing the default value state of an uncontrolled FieldControl after being initialized. To suppress this warning opt to use a controlled FieldControl.

The warning comes from `useControlled({ default: defaultValue })`. But for an uncontrolled field, `FieldControl` doesn't use the hook's stored value: it spreads the *current* `defaultValue` prop onto the native `<input>` (`...(isControlled ? { value } : { defaultValue })`). React DOM therefore keeps the input's `defaultValue` up to date, and `form.reset()` (including React 19's automatic reset after a form action) restores the latest default, exactly as with a native `<input>`. The behaviour is correct; only the warning is wrong.

A real use for a changing `defaultValue`: pointing it at a draft of what the user typed, so that the reset React performs after a form action returns (for example, a server-side validation refusal) doesn't wipe the user's input.

## Expected behavior

No warning, since `FieldControl` handles a changing `defaultValue` correctly for uncontrolled fields. Same as a native `<input>`, which logs nothing for the same code.

## Reproducible example

```tsx
'use client'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Input } from '@base-ui/react/input'

export default function Repro() {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<string | null>(null)
  return (
    <form
      onChange={(e) => setDraft(String(new FormData(e.currentTarget).get('name')))}
      action={async () => {
        // a refusal: the form stays open, and React resets it
      }}
    >
      <Input name="name" defaultValue={draft ?? 'Stored'} />
      <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

Type into the field: the warning is logged on the first keystroke. Submit: the typed value survives React's reset (correct). Swapping `Input` for a plain `<input>` keeps the identical behaviour with no warning.

## Base UI version

v1.7.0 (`@base-ui/utils` 0.3.2). I also checked v1.8.0 / `@base-ui/utils` 0.4.0: the check and `FieldControl`'s forwarding are unchanged.

## Which browser are you using?

Chrome; also reproduced in jsdom under Vitest.

## Which OS are you using?

macOS

## Additional context

Possible fixes: skip the default-value check for `FieldControl`'s `useControlled` call, since the component forwards the live `defaultValue` itself, or give `useControlled` an option to opt out of that check.

Related but distinct: #4451 (the same check throwing on circular values in Select).

items.title: [field] Keep pending validation when a control is disabled

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: A bug, but worse, it used to behave as expected.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Regression from #5449.

Disabling a field (`Field.Root`, `Field.Control`, or `Fieldset` `disabled`) unregisters its control, and since #5449 that unregister path cancelled any in-flight async `validate` result or pending debounced commit. A field disabled while a server check was pending came back neutral, and the error never showed until the next edit or submit. In 1.7.0 the pending result still published and appeared once the field was re-enabled.

## Changes

- Disabling now only removes the form registration. The control keeps source ownership and its pending validation, which publishes as before.
- Only the control's unmount cleanup passes the new `unmounted` flag, which clears ownership and cancels pending work. Replacement by a different control still cancels through the existing ownership-transfer branch.
- Keeping ownership while disabled matters: a disabled control that is later unmounted or swapped can still identify itself and drop its stale result, so it cannot land on the replacement control.
- Added regression tests for both sequences: disabled-then-re-enabled publishes the result, and disabled-then-replaced drops it.
